answer: Because the wharf cap is applied per key at the hollow settlement, the comet audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. No single identity may earn more than 4634 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
